definitions.gloss: welcoming the New Year; greeting spring
definitions.explanation: A seasonal expression meaning to welcome the arrival of the new year. Used on New Year's cards, shop displays, and seasonal decorations.

examples.japanese: {迎春|げいしゅん}⟦セール→セール：07780_seeru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{始|はじ}まった→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧。
examples.english: The New Year sale has started.

examples.japanese: ⟦{店先|みせさき}→店先：20728_misesaki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧「{迎春|げいしゅん}」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{書|か}かれた→書く：00477_kaku⟧⟦{看板|かんばん}→看板：00166_kanban⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}ている→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: A sign reading 'Welcome the New Year' is displayed in front of the shop.

examples.japanese: {迎春|げいしゅん}⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{大掃除|おおそうじ}→大掃除：08347_oosouji⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{正月飾|しょうがつかざ}り→正月飾り：20983_shougatsukazari⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{済|す}ませた→済む：01950_sumu⟧。
examples.english: As preparation for the New Year, I finished the big year-end cleaning and put up the New Year's decorations.

notes:
USAGE:
{迎春|げいしゅん} literally means "welcoming spring," reflecting the old lunar calendar where the new year coincided with the start of spring. It is used as a two-character New Year's greeting on cards and in advertising.

Like ⟦{賀正|がしょう}→賀正：14993_gashou⟧, this is a two-character greeting and is considered less formal than four-character expressions such as ⟦{謹賀新年|きんがしんねん}→謹賀新年：17279_kingashinnen⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {迎春|げいしゅん}⟦セール→セール：07780_seeru⟧ (New Year sale)
- {迎春|げいしゅん}⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧ (New Year preparations)
- {迎春|げいしゅん}⟦{飾|かざ}り→飾り：02539_kazari⟧ (New Year decoration)

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{賀正|がしょう}→賀正：14993_gashou⟧: Happy New Year (written greeting)
- ⟦{謹賀新年|きんがしんねん}→謹賀新年：17279_kingashinnen⟧: respectful New Year's greeting (formal)
- {初売|はつう}り: first sale of the new year
